caseIntro: A closer look at the engineering decisions, service boundaries and operational concerns behind the platform. This study describes architecture, without claiming user counts, revenue or unprovided performance metrics.

caseSections.title: Overview
caseSections.body: Baruq is a multi-vendor marketplace with web and PWA clients. Its engineering concerns span products, sellers, baskets, orders, payment, shipping and identity. The case study focuses on how these responsibilities connect while retaining clear ownership.

caseSections.title: Architecture
caseSections.body: Microservices own their data through a database-per-service approach. Clients enter through an API Gateway rather than coupling directly to every internal service. Service boundaries should reflect business capabilities, with explicit APIs and messages between them.

caseSections.title: Authentication & Authorization
caseSections.body: Centralized identity uses Duende and the OAuth 2.0 / OpenID Connect model. JWT validation protects API access; API scopes describe access boundaries, while authorization checks decide which operations a caller can perform. PKCE protects the authorization-code exchange for public clients.

caseSections.title: Messaging
caseSections.body: RabbitMQ and MassTransit support event-driven communication. Events communicate changes between service boundaries. An event consumer needs to handle duplicate delivery and failure explicitly; messaging is a reliability concern as well as a transport choice.

caseSections.title: Service Communication
caseSections.body: gRPC supports explicit synchronous service contracts where a response is needed in the current operation. Asynchronous messaging serves work that can proceed independently. The choice depends on consistency needs, latency and what should happen when the other service is unavailable.

caseSections.title: Product & Seller Architecture
caseSections.body: Product maintains a local SupplierReadModel instead of reading the Seller database directly. This keeps Seller data ownership intact and lets Product answer its own queries. The local model is a projection of the seller information Product needs, rather than a second source of truth.

caseSections.title: Payment
caseSections.body: The payment boundary separates order intent from gateway interaction. Checkout needs to retain order identity through retries and callbacks. A redirect alone is not evidence of payment: the application must use server-verified payment state.

caseSections.title: Shipping
caseSections.body: Shipping connects address information, seller ownership and the order workflow. Quotes and selected delivery methods need explicit identifiers so a checkout can be validated against the services responsible for those decisions.

caseSections.title: Infrastructure
caseSections.body: Docker packages application services for Linux environments. Traefik provides reverse-proxy routing and participates in the TLS termination path. DNS, certificates and forwarding configuration must align with application endpoints and authentication redirect URLs.

caseSections.title: Engineering Challenges
caseSections.body: The interesting problems live between boundaries: preserving product and variant identity, keeping seller data decoupled, distinguishing synchronous failure from delayed events, and tracing identity or deployment problems across the request path. Each requires explicit contracts and end-to-end validation.

about.title: Engineering complex systems, one problem at a time.
about.lead: I'm a Senior .NET Backend Engineer and Software Architect based in Tehran, Iran, with 10 years of professional experience building enterprise and distributed software systems.
paragraphs: My work spans backend engineering, microservices architecture, authentication, event-driven systems, infrastructure, and production troubleshooting.
I enjoy solving complex engineering problems where application code, distributed services, security, and infrastructure meet.

principles.title: Clarity before complexity
principles.text: Understand the problem and the ownership boundaries before introducing another abstraction.

principles.title: Contracts before assumptions
principles.text: Make data, identity, failure behavior and responsibility explicit between services.

principles.title: Validate the whole path
principles.text: A local fix is only useful when the complete workflow behaves correctly.

processTitle: How I solve difficult engineering problems.

process.title: Understand
process.text: Define the behavior, constraints and the impact.

process.title: Investigate
process.text: Follow the evidence across the system.

process.title: Find the root cause
process.text: Separate the symptom from the mechanism.

process.title: Implement
process.text: Make the change with clear boundaries.

process.title: Validate
process.text: Verify the full workflow and failure paths.
